shares_override.reason: DATA_GAP:shares — diluted shares missing for 2023, 2024, 2025 in companyfacts. The consolidated continuing operations in the FY2025 10-K are the Formula One Group (Liberty Live and Liberty SiriusXM are presented as discontinued operations), so the Formula One Group diluted WASO is the denominator that matches the engine's continuing-ops OE numerator and the FWONA/FWONK price. name: Liberty Media Corporation — Formula One Group
sector: Media & Entertainment — live sports rights (Formula 1, MotoGP)
moat_justification: Strong, contract-backed sports-rights moat: Formula 1 is the exclusive FIA world championship with all 11 teams locked into the ninth Concorde Agreement through 2030, a scarce 24-race calendar, long-dated race-promotion/media/sponsorship contracts and demonstrated pricing power (Las Vegas GP extended through 2037, Pirelli through 2028, MotoGP team/manufacturer agreements through 2031); MotoGP (acquired July 2025) adds the second global motorcycle championship under the same playbook. Capped at 7, not higher: the teams capture the majority of the economics through prize payments, so OE margins stay thin (OE yield 3.57% at the current price); growth depends on periodic media-rights and Concorde renegotiations; and the group carries real leverage (net debt 5.3x normalized OE) plus calendar/geopolitical and promoter-economics risk.
moat_for: Exclusive commercial rights to the FIA Formula 1 World Championship; all 11 teams signed the ninth Concorde Agreement (commercial + governance) through 2030
Scarce, global calendar with long-dated contracted revenue: race promotion fees, media rights and sponsorship (Las Vegas GP extended through 2037; Pirelli through 2028)
Proven pricing power — media rights, hosting fees and sponsorship have compounded through successive renewals; U.S. audience growth still scaling
Second championship under the same model: MotoGP (closed July 3, 2025), with all manufacturers/teams re-signed through 2031
Asset-light rights model: promoters and teams fund the venues and the cars; Liberty funds neither
moat_against: Teams take the majority of the prize fund — the rights holder's OE margin is structurally thin (base OE $2.98/share on $4,482M FY2025 revenue)
Economics reset at each Concorde / media-rights cycle; teams and manufacturers hold real bargaining power (next reset into 2031)
Leverage: net debt $4,045M is 5.3x normalized OE (engine diagnostics), including MotoGP acquisition debt — levered OE can shrink fast in a downturn
Calendar and geopolitical exposure: the 2026 Bahrain GP had to be rescheduled (to Malaysia in October) and H1 2026 F1 revenue fell 15% on race timing
Diluted WASO is rising (240M in 2023 to 258M in 2025 per the FY2025 10-K) — per-share growth trails group growth
Single-franchise concentration post-Liberty Live split-off (Dec 15, 2025): no diversification left inside the tracker
one_liner: Elite sports-rights franchise, moat 7/10 — but at $83.32 the OE yield is only 3.57% (base OE $2.98/share, net debt 5.3x normalized OE), so even the super-bull case earns just 14.2% IRR; weighted IRR is 8.07% with IV@15% $34.23, and it clears the 15% hurdle only below ~$34.
